purpose: How the SEO and Growth agents plan, write and link pages for CVTara (owner brief 2026-11-12). Every page must say honestly which job-search problem CVTara solves and give real value before asking for sign-up.
rules: One page per search intent. Before planning a page, check the backlog target and Search Console: if another page already ranks for the search, improve that page instead of making a new one.

No thin or near-copy pages. A generated page needs at least three facts that belong only to it (role-specific skills, a filled example, local or industry detail). Pages without them stay noindex,follow, like the city pages without a local note.
Never invent numbers, salaries, statistics, reviews or results. Use only figures from Search Console, CVTara's own data or a named official source with a link.
No pages attacking or naming competitors; write neutral 'how to choose' guides instead (owner decision 2026-11-12).
Never mention AI on public pages; never promise jobs, interviews, shortlisting or an ATS pass.
Every page states the problem in the searcher's words, the honest fix, and where CVTara helps (free first, paid only when it adds something).
pageTemplate: H1
The search in natural words, e.g. 'Resume for {role} freshers in India'. One H1 only.
Short answer
40-60 words directly under the H1 that answer the search on their own. Answer engines quote this block.
Who this is for
One line naming the reader (fresher, 2-5 years, career switcher) and the problem.
Steps
3-7 numbered steps the reader can follow today.
Filled example
A real, fictional-name example (bullets, summary or answer) specific to this page. This is the page's unique value.
Table
A comparison or checklist table where it helps (format vs format, do vs avoid, skills by level).
Common mistakes
3-5 mistakes recruiters see for this role or situation, with the fix.
India specifics
CTC, notice period, CGPA/percentage, campus or government rules only when they apply, with an official link.
FAQ
3-6 questions taken from Search Console queries and real customer questions, each answered in 2-3 sentences. FAQPage data only when the questions are visible on the page.
Related links
Link up to the pillar, across to 3 sibling pages and to the matching free tool, with descriptive anchor text (never 'click here').
CTA
One primary action matched to intent (informational: free check or template; commercial: build or tailor; transactional: plans). One soft secondary link.
Metadata
Title up to 50 characters before ' | CVTara', starting with the search; description 120-155 characters saying what the page gives and the next step.
Structured data
WebPage or Article + BreadcrumbList; FAQPage when the FAQ is visible; Organization and WebSite only on the home and About pages.
Trust
Who wrote or reviewed it (CVTara team, HR background), the reviewed date when a person really reviewed it, and links to official sources.
aiSearch: Put a self-contained answer of 40-60 words right under each H2 question; answer engines lift these blocks.
Use the entity names people use: CVTara, ATS (applicant tracking system), CTC, CGPA, campus placement, notice period. Define each once.
Prefer lists and tables for steps, comparisons and checklists; keep one idea per paragraph.
State facts with their source and date (official notification, government site). Do not state numbers without a source.
Keep the brand facts identical everywhere: name CVTara, made by an HR team in Bangalore, one-time payment, 7-day refund if unused, support@cvtara.com.
Keep llms.txt, the About page, Organization data and social profiles saying the same thing.
Record monthly checks of how answer engines describe CVTara in Growth > AI visibility; fix wrong facts at the source page.
